The near-infrared (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L'$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M'$</tex> bands) images reveal circumstellar structures around LkH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> 234 in detail. Eight young stellar object (YSO) candidates (Object B, C, D, E, F, G, NW1, and NW2) were detected at 2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$,''$</tex>–11<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$''$</tex> from LkH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> 234. Objects B and C are likely variable stars, which is consistent with a young evolutionary status. Three objects (LkH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> 234, NW1, and NW2) were identified in the 11.8<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \mu$</tex>m (SiC) and 17.65<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \mu$</tex>m images obtained with the Long Wavelength Spectrometer (LWS) on the Keck Telescope. NW1 and NW2 are thought to be embedded young stars. We suggest that NW1, and not LkH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> 234, is the source illuminating the reflection nebula west of LkH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> 234, although Object G may be another candidate. In our images, these objects are located at the center of the 2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \mu$</tex>m polarization, and NW1 resides at the center of a monopolar cavity. The SED of NW1 suggests that it is a YSO with a spectral type of B6–B7. Object F and G were discovered by our observations at 1<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$''\!\!\!.$</tex>9 and 2<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$''\!\!\!.$</tex>3, respectively, from LkH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> 234, and their proximity to LkH<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha $</tex> 234 suggests that they may be its lower-mass companions.

articleTitle: Suzaku and XMM-Newton Observations of the Fornax Cluster: Temperature and Metallicity Distribution
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: Suzaku observed a central region and five offset regions within 0.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ r_{180}$</tex> in the Fornax cluster, a nearby poor cluster, and XMM-Newton mapped the cluster with 15 pointings out to 0.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ r_{180}$</tex> . The distributions of O, Mg, Si, S, and Fe in the intracluster medium (ICM) were studied with Suzaku, and those of Fe and temperature were studied with XMM. The temperature of the ICM gradually decreases with the radius from 1.3 keV at 0.04 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ r_{180}$</tex> to 1 keV at 0.2–0.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ r_{180}$</tex> . If the new solar abundances of Lodders et al. (2003), ApJ, 591, 1220) and a single-temperature plasma model are adopted, O, Mg, Si, S, and Fe show similar abundances: 0.4–0.6 solar within 0.02–0.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ r_{180}$</tex> . This Fe abundance is similar to those at 0.1–0.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ r_{180}$</tex> in rich clusters and other groups of galaxies. At 0.2–0.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ r_{180}$</tex>, the Fe abundance becomes 0.2–0.3 solar. A two-temperature plasma model yields ICM abundances that are higher by a factor of 1.2–1.5, but give similar abundance ratios among O, Mg, Si, S, and Fe. The northern region has a lower ICM temperature and higher brightness and Fe abundance, whereas the southern region has a higher ICM temperature and lower brightness and Fe abundance. These results indicate that the cD galaxy may have traveled from the north because of recent dynamical evolution. The cumulative oxygen- and iron-mass-to-light ratios (OMLR and IMLR) within 0.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ r_{180}$</tex> are an order of magnitude lower than those of rich clusters and some relaxed groups of galaxies. Past dynamical evolution might have hindered the strong concentration of hot gas in the Fornax cluster's central region. Scatter in the IMLR and similarity in the element abundances in the ICM of groups and clusters of galaxies indicate early metal synthesis.

articleTitle: Discovery of Gas Bulk Motion in the Galaxy Cluster Abell 2256 with Suzaku
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The results from Suzaku observations of the galaxy cluster Abell 2256 are presented. This cluster is a prototypical and well-studied merging system, exhibiting substructures both in the X-ray surface brightness and in the radial velocity distribution of member galaxies. There are main and sub components separated by 3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overset{''}{.}$</tex> 5 in the sky and by about 2000 km s <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> in radial-velocity peaks of the member galaxies. In order to measure the Doppler shifts of iron K-shell lines from the two gas components by the Suzaku XIS, the energy scale of the instrument was carefully evaluated and found to be calibrated well. A significant shift of the radial velocity of the sub component gas with respect to that of the main cluster was detected. All three XIS sensors show the shift independently and consistently among the three. The difference is found to be 1500 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex> 300 (statistical) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex> 300 (systematic) km s <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> . The X-ray determined absolute redshifts of, and hence the difference between, the main and sub components are consistent with those of member galaxies in the optical band. The observation indicates robustly that the X-ray emitting gas is moving together with galaxies as a substructure within the cluster. These results along with other X-ray observations of gas bulk motions in merging clusters are discussed.

articleTitle: In-Orbit Performance of MAXI Gas Slit Camera (GSC) on ISS
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We report on the in-orbit performance of the Gas Slit Camera (GSC) on the MAXI (Monitor of All-sky X-ray Image) mission carried on the International Space Station (ISS). Its commissioning operation, which started on 2009 August 8, confirmed the basic performances of the effective area in the energy band of 2–30 keV, the spatial resolution of the slit-and-slat collimator and detector with 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^\circ\!\!\!.$</tex> 5 FWHM, the source visibility of 40–150 seconds for each scan cycle, and the sky coverage of 85% per 92-minute orbital period and 95% per day. The gas gains and read-out amplifier gains have been stable within 1%. The background rate is consistent with the past X-ray experiments operated at a similar low-earth orbit if its relation with the geomagnetic cutoff rigidity is extrapolated to high latitude. We also present the status of the in-orbit operation and a calibration of the effective area and the energy response matrix using Crab-nebula data.

articleTitle: Astrometry of H$_{2}$ O Masers in Nearby Star-Forming Regions with VERA. IV. L 1448 C
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We have carried out multi-epoch VLBI observations with VERA (VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry) of 22 GHz H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> O masers associated with a Class 0 protostar, L 1448 C, in the Perseus molecular cloud. The maser features trace the base of a collimated bipolar jet driven by one of the infrared counter parts of L 1448 C, named as L 1448 C(N) or L 1448-mm A. We detected possible evidence for apparent acceleration and precession of the jet according to the three-dimensional velocity structure. Based on phase-referencing VLBI astrometry, we successfully detected an annual parallax of the H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> O maser in L 1448 C to be 4.31<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex> 0.33 milliarcseconds (mas), which corresponds to a distance of 232<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex> 18 pc from the Sun. The present result is in good agreement with that of another H<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}$</tex> O maser source, NGC 1333 SVS 13, in the Perseus molecular cloud, 235 pc. It is also consistent with the photometric distance, 220 pc. Thus, the distance to the western part of the Perseus molecular cloud complex would be constrained to be about 235 pc, rather than a larger value, 300 pc, previously reported.

articleTitle: Near-Ultraviolet and Visible Spectroscopy of HAYABUSA Spacecraft Re-Entry
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: HAYABUSA is the first spacecraft ever to land on and lift off from any celestial body other than the moon. The mission, which returned asteroid samples to the Earth while overcoming various technical hurdles, ended on 2010 June 13, with the planned atmospheric re-entry. In order to safely deliver the sample return capsule, the HAYABUSA spacecraft ended its 7-year journey in a brilliant ``artificial fireball'' over the Australian desert. Spectroscopic observation was carried out in the near-ultraviolet and visible wavelengths between 3000 Å and 7500 Å at 3–20 Å resolution. Approximately 100 atomic lines such as Fe I, Mg I, Na I, Al I, Cr I, Mn I, Ni I, Ti I, Li I, Zn I, O I, and N I were identified from the spacecraft. Exotic atoms such as Cu I, Mo I, Xe I and Hg I were also detected. A strong Li I line (6708 Å) at a height of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>55 km originated from the onboard Li-Ion batteries. The FeO molecule bands at a height of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>63 km were probably formed in the wake of the spacecraft. The effective excitation temperature as determined from the atomic lines varied from 4500 K to 6000 K. The observed number density of Fe I was about 10 times more abundant than Mg I after the spacecraft explosion. N<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}^{+}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1^-$</tex>) bands from a shock layer and CN violet bands from the sample return capsule's ablating heat shield were dominant molecular bands in the near-ultraviolet region of 3000–4000 Å. OH(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>–<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>) band was likely to exist around 3092 Å. A strong shock layer from the HAYABUSA spacecraft was rapidly formed at heights between 93 km and 83 km, which was confirmed by detection of N<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$_{2}^{+}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1^-$</tex>) bands with a vibration temperature of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>13000 K. Gray-body temperature of the capsule at a height of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>42 km was estimated to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim\ $</tex>2437 K which is matched to a theoretical prediction. The final message of the HAYABUSA spacecraft and its sample return capsule are discussed through our spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Thermal Structure of a Protoplanetary Disk around HD 163296: A Study of Vertical Temperature Distribution by CO Emission Lines
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: This paper presents observations of a protoplanetary disk around the Herbig Ae star HD 163296 in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{12}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 1–0), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{12}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 3–2), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 1–0), and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 3–2) emission lines. Double-peaked emission profiles originating from the rotating circumstellar disk were detected in all of the lines. The disk parameters were estimated from model calculations in which the radial distribution of the temperature or surface density inside the disk had a power-law form. The surface density should be sufficiently high so that the disk is optically thick for all of the CO lines, as discussed in previous studies based on interferometric observations. The temperature and outer radius of the disk were also confirmed to be consistent with the previous results. Taking advantage of the difference in the position of the photosphere among the CO lines, we revealed the temperature distribution in the vertical direction. The temperature of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{12}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 3–2) emitting region is about twice higher than that of any other CO emitting region; the former is 58.5<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>9.5 K, while the latter is 31<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex>15 K at 100 AU from the central star, suggesting that there are at least two distinct temperature regions. The best-fit temperature for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{13}$</tex>CO (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 1–0) that should trace the deepest region of the disk is even lower, implying that there is also a different temperature region deep inside of the disk. Such a vertical temperature distribution in a disk was identified both in T Tauri and Herbig Ae stars (e.g., DM Tau, AB Aur, and HD 31648), and this should be a common feature in protoplanetary disks.

articleTitle: Propagation of Moreton Waves
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: With the Flare-Monitoring Telescope (FMT) and Solar Magnetic Activity Research Telescope (SMART) at Hida observatory of Kyoto University, 13 events of Moreton waves were captured at Hα center, Hα±0.5 Å, and Hα±0.8 Å wavebands since 1997. With such samples, we have studied the statistical properties of the propagation of Moreton waves. Moreton waves were all restricted in sectorial zones with a mean value of 92°. However, their accompanying EIT waves, observed simultaneously with SOHO/EIT at extreme-ultraviolet wavelength, were very isotropic with a quite extended scope of 193°. The average propagation speeds of the Moreton waves and the corresponding EIT waves were 664 km s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and 205 km s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, respectively. Moreton waves propagated either under large-scale close magnetic flux loops, or firstly in the sectorial region where two sets of magnetic loops separated from each other and diverged, and then stopped before the open magnetic flux region. The location swept by Moreton waves had a relatively weak magnetic field as compared to the magnetic fields at their sidewalls. The ratio of the magnetic flux density between the sidewall and the path falls in the range of 1.4 to 3.7 at a height of 0.01 solar radii. Additionally, we roughly estimated the distribution of the fast magnetosonic speed between the propagating path and sidewalls in an event on 1997 November 3, and found a relatively low-fast magnetosonic speed in the path. We also found that the propagating direction of Moreton waves coincided with the direction of filament eruption in a few well-observed events. This favors an interpretation of the “Piston” model, although further studies are necessary for any definitive conclusion.

articleTitle: Widely Extended [O III] 88μm Line Emission around the 30 Doradus Region Revealed with AKARI FIS-FTS
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: We present a distribution map of the far-infrared [O III] 88 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>m line emission around the 30 Doradus (30 Dor) region in the Large Magellanic Cloud obtained with the Fourier Transform Spectrometer of the Far-Infrared Surveyor on board AKARI. The map reveals that the [O III] emission is widely distributed by more than 10' around the super star cluster R 136, implying that the 30 Dor region is affluent with interstellar radiation field that is hard enough to ionize O<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{2+}$</tex>. The observed [O III] line intensities are as high as (1–2) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-6}$</tex> W m<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-2}$</tex> sr<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> on the peripheral regions 4'–5' away from the center of 30 Dor, which requires gas densities of 60–100 cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3}$</tex>. However, the observed size of the distribution of the [O III] emission is too large to be explained by massive stars in the 30 Dor region enshrouded by clouds with a constant gas density of 10<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{2}$</tex> cm<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-3}$</tex>. Therefore, the surrounding structure is likely to be highly clumpy. We also find a global correlation between the [O III] and the far-infrared continuum emission, suggesting that the gas and dust are well mixed in the highly ionized region where the dust survives in clumpy dense clouds shielded from energetic photons.

articleTitle: Suzaku Observations of Iron K-Lines from the Intracluster Medium of the Coma Cluster
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The Coma cluster was observed with the X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (XIS) onboard Suzaku in six pointings, including the central X-ray peak region, 14 ' west offset region, 30 ' and 34 ' north–west offset regions, and 44 ' and 60 ' south–west offset regions. Owing to its lower background level, Suzaku has better sensitivity to Fe K <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> lines than other satellites. Using precise Fe line measurements, we studied the temperature structure, possible bulk motions, and iron abundance distributions in the intracluster medium (ICM). The observed spectra were well-represented by a single-temperature model; a two- or three- temperature model did not improve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi^2$</tex> substantially. The temperature, derived from K <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> line ratios of H-like and He-like Fe, agrees with those derived from the single-temperature model. Because the line ratio is a steep function of temperature, the consistency supports the accuracy of temperature measurements conducted with Suzaku. Within the 34 ' region, the redshift derived from the central energy of the He-like Fe line is consistent with that from optical observations, within a calibration error of 18 eV or 818 km s <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> in the line of sight. This value is smaller than the sound velocity of the ICM, which is 1500 km s <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{-1}$</tex> . The central energy of Fe lines at the 44 ' offset region around the NGC 4839 subcluster is also consistent with those within the 34 ' region. These results on the temperature and velocity structure suggest that the core of the cluster is in a relaxed state, and non-thermal electrons relevant to the radio halo are accelerated by intracluster turbulence rather than large-scale shocks. The Fe abundance is almost constant at 0.4 solar within the 34 ' region, and decreases with radius. This value is slightly lower than those of other clusters, which means that the gas had been mixed well during a past merger associated with the growth of the cluster.

Author Keywords: galaxies: clusters: individual (Abell 1656, the Coma cluster)

articleTitle: Peculiarly Narrow SED of GRB 090926B with MAXI and Fermi/GBM
publicationTitle: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan
abstract: The monitor of the all-sky X-ray image (MAXI) Gas Slit Camera (GSC) on the International Space Station (ISS) detected a gamma-ray burst (GRB) on 2009, September 26, GRB 090926B. This GRB had extremely hard spectra in the X-ray energy range. Joint spectral fitting with the Gamma-ray Burst Monitor on the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope shows that this burst had a peculiarly narrow spectral energy distribution, which can be represented by a Comptonized blackbody model. This spectrum can be interpreted as photospheric emission from a low baryon-load GRB fireball. Calculating the parameter of the fireball, we found the size of the base of the flow to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_0$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> (4.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex> 0.9) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times$</tex> 10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{9}\ Y'^{-3/2}\ $</tex> cm, the Lorentz factor of the plasma is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex><tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> (110 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ \pm\ $</tex> 10) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ Y'^{\ 1/4}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Y'$</tex> is a ratio between the total fireball energy and the energy in the blackbody component of the gamma-ray emission. This <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_0$</tex> is a factor of a few times larger, and the Lorentz factor of 110 is smaller by also factor of a few than other bursts that have blackbody components in the spectra.
